title: Use only one contentinfo landmark per page
summary: The page has more than one contentinfo landmark. Keep one site-wide footer and change any other footer to a non-landmark element.
problem: The page exposes two or more contentinfo landmarks. A <footer> that is not inside <article>, <aside>, <main>, <nav> or <section> is treated as the page's contentinfo landmark, as is any element with role="contentinfo". A page should have only one.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users who jump between landmarks expect one contentinfo area for site-wide details such as contact information and legal links. Two of them make the landmark list ambiguous and cost extra time to sort out.
steps: List every <footer> and every role="contentinfo" in the page source and decide which one is the real site footer.
Keep that one as the only top-level <footer>.
Move any other footer inside the <article> or <section> it belongs to, where it describes only that content, or change it to a <div>.
Check that included templates and plugins do not each print their own top-level footer.
before:
Spring sale

Raised beds, compost and tools.

Prices include VAT.

Fernwood Garden Supply, 12 Mill Lane
after:
Spring sale

Raised beds, compost and tools.

Prices include VAT.

Fernwood Garden Supply, 12 Mill Lane
whyItMatters: This is a best practice, not a WCAG failure. Landmarks act as a map of the page for assistive technology, and duplicates make that map less reliable. It often also reveals a template that outputs its footer twice.
howToCheck: Search the rendered page source for <footer and role="contentinfo". Only one should sit outside of main, article, aside, nav and section. A landmarks extension should list a single contentinfo.
